summary: Iter-108 comprehensive audit of OurRealm Global Access Control (founder-only control plane + centralized SERVER-SIDE middleware enforcement). Backend pytest 27/27 PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_access_control_iter108.py covering: (1) Control plane: founder can GET panel with 11 features + 10 modes + schedules list; support admin (support/Password1$) gets 403 on ALL /api/admin/access-control/* incl. GET/PATCH/impact/preview-as/audit (no ordinary-admin bypass); tftwo also 403. (2) view_only: GET /api/responsibility-center/mine → 200; POST /create → 423 with detail.code=view_only; action-GETs containing 'export' substring → 423. (3) hidden: regular user 404 (no body leakage), founder bypass 200. (4) maintenance: 503 with founder-set detail.message echoed exactly. (5) admin_only: tftwo 403, support 200. (6) founder_only: support 403, founder 200. (7) invite_only: PUT invited=[tftwo] → tftwo 200, auditcheckreal 403 code=invite_required. (8) custom rules: allow_reads=T/allow_writes=F → reads 200, writes 423 code=custom_restricted. (9) Sub-feature isolation: orai_voice→maintenance blocks /api/orai/voice/library (503) but RC untouched (200). (10) Master cascade: orai→emergency_lock cascades to /api/orai/voice/library (423 code=emergency_lock). (11) Emergency lock + safe restore: engaged after pre-setting RC=maintenance → all governed routes 423 → disengage → snapshot exactly restored (RC back to maintenance, orai back to full_access). (12) Public preview isolation: RC=public_preview → tftwo gets 403 on real /mine; anon GET /api/access-control/preview-demo returns 200 with ONLY demo static payload (no real usernames tftwo/stealth/auditcheckreal in body); when RC=full_access and rc_public_preview=hidden → /preview-demo returns 404. (13) Schedules: one-time (past run_at) + recurring create/list/delete/cancel all 200; DELETE marks status=canceled. (14) Allowlist: reason required (400 without); grant tftwo → 423→200 flip verified under RC=emergency_lock; DELETE revokes (200→423 flip after 4s TTL). (15) Impact preview: returns affected_users, affected_centers, cascades_to (contains all 5 orai children), routes_affected, effects{all_locked:true}. (16) Preview-as personas signed_out/regular_user/platform_admin/founder all return per-feature matrix; founder persona has visible+can_write=True for every feature. (17) Audit: rows contain actor_username, action, target, before, after, reason, at. (18) Public status: 200 both anonymously and authenticated; screen ∈ {normal,view_only,maintenance,locked,hidden,preview,invite_only}. (19) Race: 5 parallel PATCHes + 5 parallel status reads → no 500s; final mode consistent with one submitted value. FRONTEND (desktop 1920x1080 + mobile 390x844): /admin/access-control renders (admin-access-control-page found), all 11 access-card-* present, emergency-lock-btn + access-schedules-section + access-allowlist-section + access-preview-as-section + preview-persona-select + access-audit-section + access-mode-select-course_player all FOUND. Course Player mode select → view_only reveals access-review-btn-course_player (only appears once dirty) → click opens access-impact-modal with impact-users, impact-centers, impact-apply-btn → reason field + Apply → badge on card flips to view_only; reverting to Full Access via same flow works. As tftwo /responsibility-center under view_only shows access-view-only-banner (sticky amber); as founder same page shows access-bypass-chip (green). Hidden mode: tftwo's top-bar star-responsibility-center icon disappears + /responsibility-center shows access-gate-hidden. Maintenance: access-gate-maintenance shows exact founder-set custom message. /admin shows 'Global Access Control' card with link to /admin/access-control. Mobile 390x844 also shows access-view-only-banner correctly. FINAL STATE VERIFIED: all 10 features back to full_access, rc_public_preview=hidden, emergency_locked=false, invited=[], allowlist=[].
critical_code_review_comments: services/access_control.evaluate() correctly returns typed 423/403/404/503 with detail={code,message,feature,mode} for every non-full_access mode. Bypass path (founder role OR active emergency_allowlist entry) is single-source-of-truth via _is_bypass(). Clean.

middleware order in server.py: global_access_control_guard is registered BEFORE global_auth_guard, meaning the auth guard runs first (outermost). This is correct — unauthenticated users hitting governed writes get 401 from auth guard (as documented in problem statement), not a data-leaking 423.

effective_mode(): iterates parents once (no recursion) — works because current registry is only 2 levels deep. If ever nested 3+ levels, transitive cascade won't trigger. Not a bug today, worth a comment.

feature_for_path() uses substring checks like '/courses' before '/orai/memory' — since /api/responsibility-center paths never contain '/orai/memory' unless explicitly written, the order works. But NB: /api/responsibility-center/{cid}/orai/memory is checked AFTER /courses — since '/courses' isn't in memory path, still correct, but the code order should reflect priority intent explicitly (memory before courses would be safer).
emergency_lock snapshot excludes rc_public_preview and forces it to 'hidden' — correct; ensures preview never opens accidentally during a lock and restore path preserves that.

run_access_schedule_pass uses find_one_and_update({status:pending}) as an atomic claim-lock so parallel workers cannot double-execute the same one_time schedule. Recurring uses last_run_key dedup. Solid.
invited_usernames stored lowercased+trimmed via sorted set — consistent case handling.

GOVERNED_PREFIXES = ('/api/orai/','/api/responsibility-center'). Note the trailing slash on orai/ but NOT on responsibility-center — this means /api/responsibility-centerXXX would ALSO match. In practice no such route exists, but consider anchoring to '/api/responsibility-center/' or '/api/responsibility-center$'.
DEMO_PREVIEW payload is static in-memory dict — good, cannot leak DB data. /preview-demo has NO authenticated user reference. Isolation verified.
audit rows include actor_username fallback 'scheduler' for null actors — nice for scheduler-driven changes.
Race test observed no 500s under 5 parallel PATCH + 5 status reads — MongoDB $set writes are atomic per-key and cache invalidation is idempotent.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of listed selectors + flows verified on desktop+mobile

seed_data_creation: None persistent. All schedules created during test were deleted. Allowlist entries added were revoked. All feature modes flipped were restored. Audit log naturally grew by ~40 rows (expected — every mode change writes an audit row). Verified final panel snapshot matches production defaults.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Global Access Control (iter-108) is fully green on backend + frontend. Backend cache TTL = 3s → always sleep 4s+ after mode changes (helper SETTLE=4.2s in test file). Emergency lock snapshot excludes rc_public_preview (forces it to 'hidden' during lock). The middleware short-circuits when _all_open(settings) is True, so happy-path performance is one cache-hit per request. Support admin (support_admin role) is EXPLICITLY blocked from the control plane — this is by design, only founder role bypasses. GOVERNED_PREFIXES currently permit '/api/responsibility-centerXXX' to match (no trailing slash on RC prefix) — cosmetic concern only. Do not attempt to test scheduled worker in <60s — the worker sleeps 60s between passes; tests verify schedule CRUD but not runtime execution. tftwo has an active center; hidden gate hides the top-bar star icon correctly. Mobile 390x844 renders view-only banner correctly.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. One test-code (not app-code) assertion in TestPublicPreview.test_preview_demo_gated_and_isolated originally checked 'Fire Power not in body' but the demo NOTICE string literally contains 'Fire Power' in its human-readable disclaimer — assertion relaxed to check absence of real usernames + restrict top-level payload keys to demo-only set.
